fact: The Reporter says the National Bank of Ethiopia introduced two regulatory frameworks in 2020, the Payment Instrument Issuers directives and the Payment Systems Operators directive, and that firms were licensed and operating under them through 2025.
system: Payment Instrument Issuers directives and Payment Systems Operators directive (NBE, 2020)

fact: The Reporter says the 2020 Payment Systems Operators directive created four licence categories (switch, POS, ATM and payment gateway operators) under which non-bank firms such as Chapa, Arifpay, Santimpay and Kacha were licensed, and the Payment Instrument Issuers directives enabled telecom operators to launch mobile wallets such as Telebirr and M-Pesa.

Digital Policy Alert states that Ethiopia amended the National Payment System Proclamation in February 2023 and the National Bank issued an October 2023 directive on licensing payment instruments including electronic money.
system: National Payment System Proclamation / NBE directive

fact: Digital Policy Alert states that the National Bank's April 2020 directive allowed non-financial institutions such as mobile operators and fintech companies to offer mobile money.

The National Bank of Ethiopia issued a revised Licensing and Authorization of Payment Instrument Issuer Directive in late May 2025, raising daily e-money transaction limits and issuer capital to 100 million Birr.

The revised directive makes interoperability among mobile wallets mandatory and requires financial institutions to participate in the Ethiopian Instant Payment System, per the National Bank of Ethiopia via Ethiopian Monitor.

Birr Metrics reports that on 12 May 2025 the National Bank of Ethiopia repealed its previous directive on Payment Instrument Issuers and replaced it with a new regulation, with the capital requirement in force immediately.

Birr Metrics reports that Payment Instrument Issuers under the National Bank of Ethiopia's May 2025 regulation are entities licensed to issue electronic money without being banks, with minimum paid-up capital raised from 50 to 100 million birr.

Birr Metrics reports that the new directive requires all Payment Instrument Issuers to let users transfer across competing wallets, and from November 2025 to do so only through EthSwitch or other NBE-licensed operators.
National Bank of Ethiopia Directive ONPS/10/2025, issued under National Payment Systems Proclamation 718 as amended, entered into force on 12 May 2025.
The directive sets licensing, capital (Birr 100 million) and shareholding rules for payment instrument issuers, allowing telecom operators among the permitted large shareholders.

The directive requires payment instrument issuers to interoperate wallet-to-wallet through the national switch or another licensed switch operator, and all financial institutions providing digital financial services to participate in the national switch's instant payment system; in force 12 May 2025.
